lesson_title: The Idea That Rode a Camel
hook_text: The camel caravans carried salt and gold. But the most powerful thing they carried weighed nothing at all.
clip_script: It was an idea: a religion called Islam. It began in Arabia, swept across North Africa, and then, from about the ninth century, it crossed the Sahara, not with soldiers, but with merchants. Picture a West African trader. His partners across the desert pray the same prayers, follow the same rules for deals, and trust each other. Join them, and doors open across half the world. So traders became Muslim, then kings. And with Islam came something huge: writing. Arabic letters, schools, scholars, libraries. Within a few centuries, a West African city on the edge of the desert would become one of the great centres of learning on Earth. Its name? Timbuktu.
visual_style: A whiteboard camel caravan carrying glowing letters of a script alongside salt and gold; a handshake between two traders; a mud-brick mosque rising; books stacking into a library.
pacing: Mystery hook, steady build, a cliffhanger name at the end.
